articles.title: The Celestial Tourist
articles.summary: This article from the February 2000 SJAA Ephemeris outlines the San Jose Astronomical Association's activities for February and March, including multiple star parties, observational astronomy classes, and general meetings with diverse topics. It also features an in-depth review by Jay Reynolds Freeman of the Stargazer Steve 3-inch f/10 Newtonian telescope, detailing its easy setup, simple design, and surprisingly capable performance on various celestial objects like planets, nebulae, and Messier targets during several observing sessions. The author praises the inexpensive, portable telescope for its effectiveness, particularly for casual and beginner use.

articles.title: SJAA Sports New Online Names
articles.summary: The San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) has successfully secured the sjaa.net domain name for its website and email services, enhancing its online presence and accessibility for members. This move, detailed under the title "SJAA Sports New Online Names," provides a concise and mnemonic address, with the site continuing to be hosted by SEDS. The document also includes an excerpt of a telescope review, praising the Stargazer Steve Sgr-3 as a fine beginner telescope despite some challenges with its peep sight finder.

articles.title: Mooning
articles.summary: This article provides a lunar observing guide for the upcoming month, highlighting that while major events are absent, optimal viewing conditions due to high lunar elevation are expected around the 15th. The author strongly recommends exploring the western quadrant of the Moon, specifically focusing on Mare Humorum, Palus Epidemarium, and the crater Gassendi, detailing their unique rilles and features for observation around the 14th and 15th.

articles.title: Shallow Sky In February
articles.summary: This article serves as an observing guide for February, detailing planetary visibility and celestial events. It highlights good early evening viewing opportunities for Jupiter (including specific moon transits) and Saturn, while noting that Mars and Mercury are also visible but Mercury's visibility fades by month's end. Morning observers can spot Venus, and other targets include asteroid 2 Pallas and the zodiacal light, with a final reminder about Leap Day.

articles.title: The Honey Moon — Observing Tips for Lovers
articles.summary: This article, 'The Honey Moon — Observing Tips for Lovers' by Jane Houston Jones, offers advice on how to blend astronomy with romance, especially for couples or those looking to introduce a special person to stargazing. It provides practical tips for creating a romantic observing experience, covering aspects like appropriate music and food, maintaining personal space at the eyepiece, sharing telescopes, and knowing when to end the evening. The piece also highlights romantic astronomical opportunities and birthdays throughout February.

articles.title: The Central Bulge
articles.summary: The article advocates for supporting Fremont Peak State Park as a valuable resource for amateur astronomers in the South Bay, emphasizing its dark skies and comfortable observing conditions. It highlights the positive relationship between amateur astronomers, the Fremont Peak Observatory Association (FPOA), and the state park service, which facilitates public astronomy sessions. The author encourages astronomers to join FPOA, volunteer, and respect park rules to maintain this favorable impression, especially as future improvements for amateur astronomy at the park are under discussion.

articles.title: Comet Comments for February 2000
articles.summary: This article, "Comet Comments for February 2000," reviews the 56 comet discoveries of 1999, noting a significant shift to CCD imaging by programs like LINEAR and SOHO, as well as amateur teams. It provides details on newly discovered comets like Hug-Bell (1999 X1) and LINEAR (1999 Y1), and offers a modest outlook for potential bright comets in 2000, including LINEAR (1999 S4) and McNaught-Hartley (1999 T1).

articles.title: SJAA Loaner Scope Status
articles.summary: This article provides a status update on the San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) loaner telescope program, detailing which telescopes are currently available for immediate loan, those on active loan, and those with extended loan periods. It also includes a waiting list for popular scopes and thanks a donor for equipment. SJAA members interested in borrowing a scope are directed to contact Mike Koop, and general calls for article submissions and mailing list subscriptions are included.
